rationale: Root-caused the earlier negative reachability result and replaced it. The previous five-node harness cut only the leader<->majority links, leaving the partner<->majority links intact, so the partner was never isolated: it accepted the successor's entries during the partition and was already repaired before the heal, which is why it converged with zero restores. With the partition sealed on both sides the same legal history keeps the stale suffix and the follower installs the same snapshot hundreds of times without progressing. This update corrects the earlier Fact, answers the two open gaps with the cause, and registers the corrected harness as a successor experiment.

investigations.question: With a partition that truly seals the leader and one partner from the other three peers, does the legal history still reach the state in which the partner holds earlier-term entries at the successor's snapshot index, and does the partner then stay unrepairable?

knowledge.statement: Standalone correction note (the superseded entries live in an earlier batch and their ids are not resolvable here): The earlier Fact concluded that a legal multi-node history reaches the precondition but the follower does not stay unrepairable, and used that to narrow the leader-side loop. The premise behind that conclusion - that the partner was isolated - was false: only the leader<->majority links were cut, so the partner<->majority path stayed open and the partner was repaired during the partition before any rejoin happened. Correction of the earlier five-node negative result. That result was an artifact of the partition: the harness disconnected only the leader from the three majority peers and left the partner reachable from them, so the partner received the successor's entries while it was supposed to be isolated and was already at store 1..4 when the heal happened (observed as restores 0, partner store 1..4, successor store 0/0). When the same harness also disconnects partner<->majority in both directions, the legal history keeps its shape: divergent_prefix reports base_index 2, partitioned_leader_last_index 7, partner_last_index 7 and partner_store 1..7 (the partner really holds earlier-term entries beyond the successor's snapshot index), successor_snapshot reports snapshot_index 4 with successor_store 0/0 (fully compacted), and rejoin_observe reports restores_before 0, restores_early 694, restores_late 705, partner_applied_index 4, partner_last_index 7, successor_applied_index 4 and successor_commit_index 4 - the partner installed the same snapshot about 700 times in the ~1.3s window while its applied index stayed pinned at the snapshot index and its advertised last index stayed at 7.
knowledge.conditions: One process, root package '.', MakeClusterCustom with five bootstrapped nodes over InmemTransport/InmemStore, TrailingLogs=0, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=1s; the fault is a two-sided partition of {leader, partner} from the other three, later healed with FullyConnect. Frozen snapshot fd2d6988362c434e9fda87b87c5fb0df. interpretations.rationale: This batch cannot link a receipt to a fixed experiment, so the conclusion is recorded as unresolved even though the corrected construction feedback is decisive and consistent. Answers to the open gaps: (a) gap about how the diverged peer was reconciled - it was never isolated, because the partition cut only leader<->majority links, so the partner accepted the successor's entries while the partition was in place and had already been repaired before the heal; sealing partner<->majority removes that repair entirely. (b) gap about which node supplied the repairing entries - the successor did, over the still-open partner link; once those links are cut, neither the successor (store 0/0 after compaction) nor any other node can replace the partner's suffix, and the follower installs the same snapshot about 700 times in ~1.3s while its advertised last index stays at 7 and its applied index stays at the snapshot index. Consequence for the finding: the asserted single-peer loop witness (CheckRun 7772ad1b5b154d498a27a79806bb0ea7) is no longer an isolated configuration - the same non-progress and snapshot re-send cycle is now reproduced by a legal five-node history in which the precondition was produced by real producers (the partitioned leader's own AppendEntries to the single partner) rather than seeded, and the earlier narrowing of that claim is withdrawn as an artifact of an incomplete partition. The retained five-node receipt CheckRun b9b56ddf3d7d43319db460b87846f71f is retained as a superseded harness result whose cause is now explained, not as counterevidence.
counterevidence: The superseded negative result (restores 0, partner store 1..4) is explained by the open partner<->majority links, so it no longer counts against the loop's reachability.
Reachability here is still shown by construction feedback rather than by a receipt in this batch; the corrected harness must be executed to make it evidence.
limitations: The corrected harness has not yet been executed by the controller; the numbers quoted are non-retained local runs (two consistent runs), so no measured conclusion is asserted.
One configuration only (five nodes, TrailingLogs=0, equal 1s timeouts, in-process transports); other settings such as default TrailingLogs were not sampled.
The harness still does not instrument RPC traffic, so the ~700 installs are counted through the follower FSM's Restore count rather than on the wire.

scope.description: Five-node legal history with a two-sided partition of {leader, partner} from the other three peers, the partitioned leader replicating uncommitted commands to the partner only, a successor elected by the majority that commits its own entry at the first divergent index and snapshots there with TrailingLogs=0, then a heal; observations cover the precondition, the successor's snapshot and store, and the partner's InstallSnapshot count and indexes over ~1.5s.
assumptions: Cutting the partner<->majority links in both directions, in addition to leader<->majority, is required for the partner to be genuinely isolated; this is the difference from the superseded harness.
The partner's FSM Restore count identifies InstallSnapshot installs without touching production logic.
Precondition guards skip rather than fail so a timing miss yields no observation.
excluded: No RPC-level instrumentation, no network transport and no default-TrailingLogs configuration.
The single-peer loop harness is not re-executed here.

experiment.prefix: MakeClusterCustom(Peers=5, Bootstrap=true, Conf{TrailingLogs:0, SnapshotInterval:1h, SnapshotThreshold:1<<20, HeartbeatTimeout/ElectionTimeout/LeaderLeaseTimeout:1s, CommitTimeout:10ms}, MakeFSMFunc returning a Restore-counting MockFSM). Wait for a leader, partner=followers[0], others=remaining three; for each other disconnect leader<->other AND partner<->other in both directions, then emit partition; base=leader.LastIndex(); fire five leader.Apply calls; wait until partner.LastIndex()>base and emit divergent_prefix with both last indexes, the partner's store bounds and the divergence index; wait up to 12s for a successor among others, apply one command, Snapshot(), and emit successor_snapshot with index, term, term of the successor, its last/applied index and store bounds; then FullyConnect() and emit a per-node timeline (state, term, last, applied, store bounds; entry terms at 3/4/5; partner Restore count and applied-command count) at 0/200/400/700/1000/1300ms, followed by rejoin_observe with the restore counts and the partner's and successor's indexes and store bounds.
experiment.responsibility: A reachability claim needs an actually isolated follower; an incomplete partition must not be read as evidence about repair.
